name: OmaWiFi - Wi-Fi Anchor
author: @HectorHache
description: Anchors this machine to one access point of a multi-AP Wi-Fi network. Shows every access point of the network you are on with its band, channel and signal, and pins the connection to the one you pick.

barWidget.description: One mark in the bar: anchored, drifted, roaming or offline, with the signal of the access point in use. Click for every access point of the network, and anchor to whichever you want.

schema.label: Network name
schema.description: Leave empty to follow the Wi-Fi network this machine is on. Set it only if you want the widget pinned to a particular network by name.

schema.label: Preferred band
schema.description: Which band the anchor aims at. 5 GHz is faster and usually has several access points of the same network to choose between; 2.4 GHz reaches further. Both lists everything and lets the ranking decide.

schema.label: Show the signal percentage
schema.description: The mark on its own says anchored, drifted, roaming or offline. The number beside it is the signal of the access point in use. Turn it off for a smaller footprint in the bar.

schema.label: Check the anchor every (seconds)
schema.description: How often the bar asks which access point the radio is on. This read does not scan, it only asks NetworkManager, so it costs nothing.

schema.label: Refresh the open panel every (seconds)
schema.description: While the panel is open. Short, because a panel is a live view: signal moves as you walk.

schema.label: Pin the band as well as the access point
schema.description: Off by default: pinning the access point alone is enough, and it lets the machine fall back to the other band when the anchored one is unreachable instead of refusing to connect. On: the profile demands this band too.

schema.label: Rank on signal alone
schema.description: Off, two coarse tie-breaks refine a close call: a channel that several neighbours also use is marked down, and so is a DFS channel, where radar detection can force a re-association. On, the strongest access point always wins outright.

schema.label: Show the ranking score
schema.description: The number the order is decided by, next to each access point. Useful when two access points report the same signal percentage.
